# Keyboard shortcuts

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen-shortcuts.py from app/keymap.js. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every Waffle command can be rebound in **Tools → Keyboard Shortcuts…** (record a chord or a sequence, detect conflicts, import or export your key map). **Help → Keyboard Shortcuts** (Shift+F1 or `?`) shows a live cheat sheet of the bindings in effect.

How to read the tables:

- `Mod` is **Ctrl** on Windows and Linux and **⌘ Cmd** on macOS (Ctrl also works there). `Ctrl` written explicitly is Ctrl everywhere.
- On macOS the **Altium-style** preset uses Command for commands such as duplicate (⌘D), find (⌘F), align left (⇧⌘L) and grid (⌘G). Use Control for wire or route (⌃W), measure (⌃M) and select net or find and replace (⌃H). macOS uses ⌘W, ⌘M and ⌘H for Close Window, Minimize and Hide. Control-click or Command-click highlights a board net. Double-click with the same modifier to cross-probe.
- Keys shown one after another, such as `P` `W`, are a **sequence**: press them one at a time, as in Altium Designer®. The status bar shows the possible next keys after a prefix.
- **Context** says where a binding applies (for example only on boards, or only while routing).
- Your bindings override preset bindings in the same context. A live sequence prefix still takes precedence over a single key. Keyboard Shortcuts flags both clashes and keys hidden by a sequence.
- Shortcuts contributed by bundled extensions apply while those extensions are enabled.
- Commands without a key are still reachable from the menus and the command palette (`Mod+Shift+P` or F1).

Presets: [Altium-style (default)](#altium-style-default), [Waffle Classic](#waffle-classic), [KiCad-like](#kicad-like), [VS Code-like](#vs-code-like), [Allegro-like](#allegro-like), [Modern (Mac)](#modern-mac), [Altium + RTS camera (WASD, edge scroll)](#altium--rts-camera-wasd-edge-scroll).

*Waffle Classic* keeps the defaults from before the Altium chord pass (R rotates, + and − zoom, Ctrl+D opens layer controls, no E, A, C or U prefixes). *KiCad-like* builds on Waffle Classic. *Allegro-like* builds on the default; *Modern (Mac)* has its own table (see [keymap-modern-mac.md](keymap-modern-mac.md)). Choose a preset in Preferences › Keyboard › Key preset or under Learn on the start page.

The *Altium-style*, *KiCad-like* and *VS Code-like* presets are named after the tools whose key habits they approximate. Waffle is not affiliated with or endorsed by Altium LLC, the KiCad project, Cadence Design Systems, Apple, Figma or Microsoft; see [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](../THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).

## Search

There is one search surface, the palette. Each key opens it with a different starting filter, shown as a chip in its field; Backspace in the empty field or a click on the chip removes the filter and searches everything. The app bar has no search field (removed 2026-11-23).

| Key (default) | Filter | Lists | Menu |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `/` | none | Everything: objects across the project, documents, commands, settings, library parts, help. | View › Search Everything… |
| `Mod+Shift+P`, F1 | Commands | Commands and settings | View › Command Palette… |
| `Mod+F` | Project | Components (designators), pins and pads, nets, ports, labels and text in every document of the project | Edit › Find… |
| `Mod+P` | Documents | The project's documents and recent files (quick open) | View › Quick Open… |
| `J C`, `Mod+Shift+O` / `J L` | Jump to object / location | Typed `@` / `:` prefixes of the same palette | Edit › Jump to… |

Find and Replace Text (`Ctrl+H` on sheets, `Mod+Shift+F`) and Find Similar Objects (`Shift+F`) keep their own dialogs. Panel filter fields filter only their panel. Before 2026-11-23 `Mod+F` was Find Text on sheets and Flip Board on boards (Flip Board stays on `V` `B` and View › Flip Board), `Mod+P` was Print (File › Print…) and `/` opened the notebook Insert palette at the pointer (Place › Insert or Search…).

## VS Code keys

VS Code habits that apply to a schematic and PCB editor. The policy, per key: the *Altium-style* default keeps Altium meanings where Altium users rely on them and adds the VS Code meaning where nothing clashes; the *VS Code-like* preset (built on the default) takes the VS Code meaning everywhere. Choose it as the **Key preset** in Preferences › Keyboard or under Learn on the start page. `Mod+1`…`Mod+9` stay selection memory.

| Key | In VS Code | Altium-style (default) | VS Code-like preset | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Mod+Shift+P / F1 | Command palette | Command palette | Command palette | Same meaning everywhere. |
| Mod+P | Quick open | Quick open | Quick open | Quick open lists the project's documents and recent files (2026-11-23; was Print, as in Altium). Print stays on File › Print…. |
| Mod+E | Quick open (Windows) | — | Quick open |  |
| Mod+Shift+O | Go to symbol in editor | Jump to object | Jump to object | Free in Altium: added to the default. |
| Mod+T | Go to symbol in workspace | — | Jump to object |  |
| Mod+G | Go to line | Set snap grid (Altium) | Jump to location | The default keeps Altium's grid; Jump to Location is also J L. |

## Allegro keys

The *Allegro-like* preset builds on the Altium-style default and adds the function keys of the Allegro PCB Editor's stock env file. Typed coordinates use the command line: press `X` (or **Edit › Coordinate Entry…**), then `x 10 20`, `ix 5`, `iy -2` or `ixy 1 2` and Enter; the point snaps and commits like a click. Values are in the display unit unless they carry one (`10mil`, `0.5mm`); relative entries start from the last point clicked or entered. Some sites ship env files with other function keys (for example F7 next, F8 oops); rebind them in Tools › Keyboard Shortcuts….

| Allegro | Allegro meaning | Key in this preset | Waffle command | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| F2 | zoom fit | F2 | Fit design | F also fits the design. Mod+0 fits the document. |
| F3 | add connect | F3 | Route (track on boards, wire on sheets) | P T, W and Ctrl+W still route. |
| F4 | show element | F4 | Properties panel | Waffle shows the picked object's details in Properties instead of a report window. |
| F5 | redraw | — | — | Waffle redraws continuously; there is nothing to refresh. F5 is left free (the default's Net colour override is on View). |
| F6 | done | F6 | Done: end the current command | Commits what the command has made and returns to Select (a route is kept, a placement is ended). |
| F7 | oops | F7 | Retract the last routing click; Undo otherwise | Backspace still retracts while routing. |
| F8, F9 | cancel | F8, F9 | Cancel the current command | Discards the unfinished route or placement and returns to Select. Next Violation stays on Tools. |
| F10 | grid toggle | F10 | Toggle visible grid |  |
| F11, F12 | zoom in, zoom out | F11, F12 | Zoom in, zoom out | On macOS, F11 is Show Desktop unless the function keys are set to standard function keys. |
| Ctrl+R | rotate 90° while moving (alias ~R angle 90) | Ctrl+R | Rotate counterclockwise | Only while something can rotate; Ctrl/⌘+R stays Rubber stamp otherwise. |
| x X Y | pick at an absolute coordinate | X, then x X Y | Coordinate entry (command line) | Typed during placement or routing; the point snaps like a click. Edit › Coordinate Entry… opens it too. |
| ix DX, iy DY | pick relative to the last pick | X, then ix / iy / ixy | Coordinate entry (command line) | Relative to the last point you clicked or entered. |
| Right-click › Done / Oops / Cancel | finish, undo a pick, abort | F6 / F7 / F8 | Done / Oops / Cancel | Waffle's right-click ends the current stage, as in Altium; the Allegro pop-up menu is not reproduced. |
| Right-click › Next | next candidate under the pointer | — | — | No equivalent: click again to cycle overlapping objects. |
| Strokes (right-drag gestures) | stroke commands (copy, move, zoom, undo…) | — | — | Right-drag pans in Waffle; there is no stroke recogniser. |
| Typed commands (add connect, slide, move, delete, show element, zoom fit…) | the command console | X, then the command | The command line maps the common ones | add connect, slide, move, delete, show element, show measure, zoom fit/in/out, grid toggle, undo, redo, done, oops, cancel. Anything else: the command palette. |
| Environment aliases / funckey | user key bindings in the env file | — | Tools › Keyboard Shortcuts… | Waffle imports VS Code keybindings, not Allegro env files. |
| Design Workflow / Options, Find and Visibility panes | the right-hand panes | — | Properties, Filter and View Configuration panels | Not key bindings. |

## Modern (Mac) keys

A ⌘-centred profile: macOS conventions first, one letter per tool as in Figma, hold Space to pan, no two-key Altium sequences, and rare commands on ⌘K chords (⌘K opens the command palette at once; press ⌘ and a second key to run a chord). The full table with the reason for each key, and what was left off, is in [keymap-modern-mac.md](keymap-modern-mac.md).
